A traffic engineering study was conducted to investigate traffic delay at urban intersections. Three types of traffic signals were studied: pretimed, semi-actuated, and fully actuated. Fifteen intersections were completely randomly assigned to one of the three types of signals. The response variable was the average stopped time per vehicle (seconds) at each intersection.

:::{.version-instructions}
The data for this study is provided in [`traffic_data.csv`](../_data/02_traffic_data.csv).

Download the data here or on Canvas and save it in your nicely organized "activities" or "data" folder!

This is what the data looks like:
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# load the packages we need for this activity
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(knitr)
library(janitor)
```
:::




:::{.version-student .version-solution}

This code below reads in the data (`read_csv()`), makes the variable names nicer in R (`clean_names()`), and makes sure sure the order of the levels
of the treatment are in a nice order for us (`factor()`).

:::{.callout-note}
`factor` is a special data type in R. This is distinct from our term "factor" in relation to study design.
:::


:::


::: {.cell version='["instructions","solution"]'}

```{.r .cell-code}
traffic_data <- read_csv("../_data/02_traffic_data.csv") |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  mutate(traffic_signal = factor(traffic_signal, 
                                levels = c("Pretimed", 
                                           "Semi-actuated", 
                                           "Fully actuated")))
```
:::
